subject: English
topic: Fill in the Blanks — Vocabulary and Grammar in Context (W10)

questions.stem: The scientist made a ________ discovery that changed the course of medicine forever.
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Landmark' means a significant, memorable achievement that marks an important stage. The sentence says the discovery 'changed the course of medicine', implying historic importance. Trap: 'trivial', 'casual', and 'minor' are all antonymous to the context — a discovery that changes medicine cannot be described with any of these words.

questions.stem: Despite his ________ efforts, he managed to complete the ambitious project before the deadline.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Despite his ... efforts' followed by 'managed to complete' implies the efforts were sustained and determined — 'persistent' (continuing firmly despite difficulty) fits. Trap: 'lazy' and 'careless' contradict both 'efforts' and the successful outcome; 'random' does not describe a quality of effort relevant to task completion.

questions.stem: The ambassador's speech was so ________ that it moved the entire audience to tears.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Eloquent' means fluent, persuasive, and powerfully expressive in speech. Moving an audience to tears indicates great emotional impact through words — eloquence. Trap: 'incoherent' (unclear) and 'monotonous' (boring) are opposite to something that moves people; 'repulsive' (disgusting) would cause a very different reaction.

questions.stem: The government ________ a new policy to curb the rapidly rising inflation in the country.
questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Implemented a new policy' means the government put the policy into action — the correct collocation for introducing and enacting a policy. Trap: 'ignored', 'avoided', and 'neglected' all suggest inaction, which contradicts the introduction of a new policy. Note: one cannot 'ignore a new policy' — the government would be the policy maker, not the ignorer.

questions.stem: His argument was well-structured but lacked concrete ________ to support his claims.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Concrete evidence' is the standard expression for factual support behind an argument. The argument 'lacked' something to 'support his claims' — only 'evidence' directly supports claims in formal reasoning. Trap: 'hypothesis' is a proposed explanation (itself an unsupported claim); 'opinion' is subjective and would weaken, not support, claims; 'suggestion' is too informal for an argument's supporting material.

questions.stem: The athlete's ________ performance at the Olympics earned her widespread acclaim.
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Stellar' means outstanding or exceptionally brilliant — consistent with earning 'widespread acclaim' at the Olympics. Trap: 'mediocre' (only average), 'average', and 'substandard' (below average) would NOT earn widespread acclaim. This tests the student's vocabulary: stellar literally means 'of or like a star', hence 'star-quality.'

questions.stem: The committee was ________ to reach a consensus because its members held ________ views on the proposed reform.
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Unable to reach a consensus' + 'divergent views' creates perfect logical cohesion: divergent (moving in different directions) views explain why consensus was impossible. Trap: 'eager/similar' contradicts the scenario (similar views would produce easy consensus); 'forced/unanimous' implies agreement was achieved; 'unwilling/complementary' is illogical — complementary views reinforce each other.

questions.stem: Although the plan seemed ________ on paper, its actual implementation proved far more ________ than anyone had anticipated.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The contrast is between appearance and reality: 'seemed ________ on paper' (positive) vs. 'proved far more ________ ' (challenging). 'Feasible' (achievable, workable) fits the positive initial assessment; 'complex' (difficult, many-layered) fits the unexpectedly hard reality. Trap: 'practical/simple' — if it seemed practical/simple, complexity would be a reasonable contrast, but 'practical on paper' is weaker than 'feasible'; 'complicated/rewarding' reverses the contrast direction.

questions.stem: The ________ of ancient manuscripts has helped historians construct a more ________ understanding of early civilizations.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Preservation of manuscripts' (keeping them safe through time) combined with 'comprehensive understanding' (thorough, wide-ranging) is the most logically and lexically coherent pair. Preservation allows historians to study primary sources; primary source access broadens their understanding. Trap: 'destruction' directly contradicts helping historians; 'translation/narrow' is contradictory (translation broadens, not narrows); 'discovery/incomplete' — 'discovery' could work, but 'incomplete understanding' is negatively framed, inconsistent with 'helped historians construct.'

questions.stem: The CEO's unilateral decision to ________ the merger without consulting the board was widely regarded as an ________ of authority.
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Approve a merger unilaterally' (without board consultation) constitutes an 'abuse of authority' — using power improperly or beyond one's sanctioned role. The word 'unilateral' signals wrongful solo action. Trap: 'reject/exercise' — one can exercise authority legitimately, but 'widely regarded as' implies criticism, ruling out neutral 'exercise'; 'announce/extension' — announcing a merger is not inherently an abuse; 'postpone/delegation' has no logical link to 'widely criticized'.
